intro.title: Garden room or garden home?
paragraphs: Since 27 July 2026 they are legally different things. A garden room (Class 3) is a home office, gym, studio or store of up to 30 m², and nobody can live in it. A garden home (Class 3A) is a detached house of 32 to 45 m² in the rear garden, lived in together with the main house.

A garden home must be occupied in conjunction with the main house. It cannot be sold or subdivided from the main house, and short-term letting is not allowed. The regulations do not limit it to family members, but it is not a separate property you can sell off.

faqs.q: Do I need planning permission for a garden home?
faqs.a: Not if it meets every one of the Class 3A conditions. If any condition is not met, planning permission is needed. We check your site first, and a Section 5 declaration from the council gives certainty.

faqs.q: Can I rent out a garden home?
faqs.a: It must be occupied in conjunction with the main house. It cannot be sold or subdivided, and short-term letting is not allowed. The regulations say nothing specific about longer-term letting, so take advice from your solicitor before relying on it.
Yes. Existing sheds count towards the 45 m² limit.

faqs.q: Can the garden home have its own water and electricity connections?
faqs.a: No. Separate utility connections are not allowed, so services run through the main house. Our costing allows for this.

faqs.q: How long does the exemption last?
faqs.a: The home must be built and finished by 31 December 2030.

faqs.q: What if my garden does not qualify?
faqs.a: Then planning permission is needed. An attached family flat is another route; it always needs planning permission and the rules are set by the county plan. Meath, for example, requires it to be attached to the house.

sections.title: The Class 3A rules in brief
paragraphs: All 20 conditions must be met. If any one is not, planning permission is needed. These are the main ones.
bullets: Detached home in the rear garden, 32 to 45 m², with existing sheds counting towards the 45 m²
Up to 4 m high with a pitched, tiled roof, or 3 m otherwise
Lived in together with the main house; cannot be sold or subdivided
The owner lives in the main house when work starts
At least 0.6 m from the boundaries
At least 25 m² of garden kept
The council is notified 14 days before work starts

sections.title: Building Regulations apply in full
paragraphs: A garden home is a new dwelling under Building Regulations. That covers fire safety, energy, ventilation, drainage and access. We design it to meet them from the first drawing.
The extension exemption cannot be used to extend a garden home later, so it is worth getting the size right at the start.

sections.title: Services through the main house
paragraphs: Because separate utility connections are not allowed, water, power and drainage run through the main house. Our costing allows for these service runs from the start.
